title: Minimal-touch proxy shim onramp for air-gapped private deployments
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Background: Multiple enterprise customers (finance + healthcare) requested a lower-friction onramp for Private/VPC air-gapped installations. They cannot open long-lived inbound tunnels and prefer a short, auditable interaction that accomplishes license exchange, preflight checks, and a minimal proxy for artifact delivery during upgrades. Current intake lanes are manual and require Sales/SE coordination; implementation time averages 6+ weeks.

Goal: Ship a Minimal-touch Proxy Shim (MTPS) pattern and delivery lane that allows customers to complete Private onramp in 48–72 hours with minimal network changes. MTPS will provide a short-lived outbound-initiated handshake, a validated compatibility shim for one-time artifact transfer, and an automated preflight checklist generator.

Success criteria / Acceptance criteria:
- Customers can complete initial connectivity handshake and preflight checks without inbound firewall exceptions in 95% of cases for supported environments (RHEL/CentOS/Ubuntu, select Windows Server).
- Average time from intake to validated deployment <72 hours for eligible customers using MTPS.
- MTPS leaves no persistent open inbound ports; audit log and KMS key exchange recorded in the customer’s SIEM/KMS logs.
- Rollout path documented: self-serve + SE-assisted lanes + fallback to full on-prem installer.

Scope in MVP:
- Lightweight shim that runs as a signed binary/container executed by customer operator for a configurable ephemeral window (default 2 hours).
- Handshake flow: customer-run agent -> outbound HTTPS to our orchestrator -> ephemeral presigned artifact URLs delivered over TLS -> automated integrity check and local validation.
- Embedded compatibility probe that generates a one-page preflight manifest (OS, firewall, curl/openssl versions, existing proxy rules) and a simple remediation checklist.
- Console surface: new ‘Onramp’ route with step-by-step guided flow, preflight report ingestion, and customer-facing ticket template for SEs.
- Telemetry: tokenized correlation id, per-step latency, failure reasons, and an aggregated readiness score shown in Console.

Out of scope (MVP):
- Full bastion or long-lived relay services.
- Windows domain-integrated installers (partial support only).
- Custom corporate proxy discovery beyond basic proxy env parsing.

Implementation notes / trade-offs:
- Security vs friction: prefer outbound-initiated ephemeral windows with signed audit artifacts rather than persistent tunnels. This reduces attack surface but requires robust transient credential exchange (short-lived JWTs + customer-supplied public key pinning).
- Transport choice: HTTPS over standard ports to maximize pass-through; fallback to S3-presigned URLs for artifact delivery to handle strict egress filters.
- Integrity: sign manifests and artifacts with HSM-backed keys; provide local fingerprint verify script to customer operator.
- Operational complexity: orchestrator must track windows and provide automatic expiry and revocation. Adds stateful responsibilities to the control plane but simplifies customer network requirements.

Rollout plan:
1) Internal alpha with 2 SE-led customers (mid-March) to validate handshake and preflight report.
2) Beta cohort (10 customers) with SE onboarding and expanded OS coverage (late March–early April).
3) GA documentation + self-serve Console lane (target 2026-04-15).

Metrics to track:
- Time-to-validated-deploy (hours)
- Preflight pass rate and most common remediation items
- Percentage of customers requiring inbound exceptions after MTPS attempt
- Post-onboard incidents attributable to onramp (target: zero critical incidents)

Open questions / risks:
- Legal/contract: do we need updated terms for ephemeral artifact access? (Legal review requested).
- Audit: customers in regulated industries may need proof of artifact retention policies; ensure artifacts are not persisted server-side beyond agreed TTL.
- Edge cases: networks with egress inspection that mangle TLS (enterprise DLP) — need fallback plans.
